chapter: Train trip with the rich sponsors
title: Sleeping in the baggage car, Baton Rouge dance and payoff
summary: The band sleeps on cots in the baggage car, wakes up back in Alexandria, stops two days in Baton Rouge to play a dance, and is paid off in Monroe.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Man, I made so much money. Dr. William give us $20 a piece to have fun with. I didn't know what to do with money then. I just put pocket that money in. I had some fun, but I didn't know nothing about spending no big money then. So we had a time. Frankie and all of them come down and enjoyed themselves. Man, so one morning, the first morning, Ed went down to see when they were going to leave. He said, all right, Ed, say, have everybody aboard for about 11 o'clock. He said, just get on the train and you know where you all sleep at. Just go on to bed because we don't know what time. We're allowed to run around there and go on to many. So we got our orders and we run all around and ramp all the streets everywhere where we want to go. I come down about nine o'clock. We all come down tired, you know, went to bed. And they left when they, let's see, we slept in the baggage car. They put a whole lot of cots in that baggage car. That's the way it was. Every man had a cot of his own. And I had a train back out there and started running. I hadn't been home in a long while in Plagman. I owned a C Plagman up there. I ain't never woke up. When I woke up, they woke me up in Alexander. All the way. Yeah, and then got on the mountain. They changed the engines at Baton Rouge Junction, but it didn't change the course. Just the engine. Pulled out on the mountain, see from the teepee to the mountain. When I woke up, I was in the Alexander. Got off and went right on home. Yeah. Rest, went down to Lee Street that evening, you know. When we got in Monroe, it was day, that's the way it was. And Dr. Williams paid off. Says, fellas, y'all sure didn't have a nice band. We stopped in Baton Rouge, took Johnson and all them, got on board and we traded them there. I believe, let me see, we was two days in Baton Rouge. We give a dance there, that's the way it was.
We stopped over there. The whole club and everybody. No, the band.

We didn't have nothing to do, we had to make a parade in Baton Rouge and bring them fellas down to the hotel. And we was through, you see. Took Johnson and them come aboard, and I got Took to fix the dance, you know. We played dance. Made nice money on that. And from Baton Rouge we come to New Orleans, you see, and back. Back to Monroe, the paid us off in Monroe. And man, you know, they didn't have no liquor in Sreeport. All of us got us one of them big, there-go baskets and bought beer and different stuff, you know. Put it in the baggage car.
